title: Hero mode: play one soldier in first person, build with blocks, command the squad
summary: Inside the unmodified 0 A.D. engine, you play one Spartan hero in first person with a Minecraft-style HUD (hearts, food, XP, a 9-slot hotbar). You place and break 4 m stone blocks that really block movement, and order your squad to follow, rally, attack, hold or take a formation. The GUI, scripts and agents send the same typed commands.

status.evidence: locally tested on Linux x86_64: 0 A.D. 0.0.26 (Ubuntu 24.04 package) headless and visual, and 0.28.0 (Ubuntu archive packages) headless
status.multiplayer: not supported: the epoch and session rules assume one simulation

profile.sandbox: none: the game process runs with your user's permissions. The lab adds limits, not isolation: only the recipe's command types are forwarded, the RL port listens on 127.0.0.1, the process gets a CPU-time cap and a wall-clock deadline, and it is stopped by its exact PID. On Linux its mods, config, logs and cache go to a lab folder.
profile.why: The mechanic needs the real engine's pathfinding, collision, combat, formations and save system. A whole engine like this does not compile to WebAssembly, and re-implementing those systems would be a lookalike, not an integration. WebAssembly fits engine-free rules (see the squad-rule world in commands.wit).

units.length: metres (0 A.D. world units); x and z are map coordinates
units.grid: blocks snap to 4 m cells: centre = (floor(v / 4) + 0.5) * 4
units.angle: radians; 0 faces +z and turning right increases it: forward = (sin a, cos a), right = (cos a, -sin a)
units.hp: the game's hit points; halfHearts = ceil(hp / maxHp * 20)
units.resources: the player's stockpile; one block costs 10 stone, halfFood = min(20, floor(food / 10))

timing.clock: the lab: headless, the game advances only when the lab calls step (RL interface /step); in visual hero mode the RL client also owns the clock (hero_lab.py steps 5 turns per second)
timing.commands_apply: in the first turn of the step they were sent before; their acks are readable right after that step

fields.src: sender name: gui-<random>, script, mcp, fixture...

refusals.stale-session: the command names another session (another game, or before a restart)
refusals.stale-epoch: the command was sent before the last load
refusals.bad-envelope: missing src, or seq is not a whole number >= 1
refusals.duplicate: seq is not above the last one seen from this src: ignored, nothing changes

envelope.resume: after a disconnect, observe and carry on from lastSeq[src] + 1; resending the last command is harmless
envelope.restart: the adapter tags every new game with a fresh session number, so commands from before a restart are refused
envelope.load: every load starts a new epoch (UmCrossover.Deserialize)

movement.recipe_does: issues stock walk orders (um-move, um-squad rally) and TurnTo (um-face)

collision.recipe_does: refuses a cell with a unit or block in it, and keeps a block only if CheckFoundation succeeds

health.recipe_does: hunger: Health.Reduce(5) every 10 s when there is no food

inventory.recipe_does: TrySubtractResources(10 stone) to place; AddResources to break or refund

persistence.recipe_does: UmCrossover.Serialize/Deserialize; Deserialize starts a new epoch

crossover_state.holds: hero, squad, formation, xp, counters, session, epoch, lastSeq, acks

effects.does: creates the hero next to your first soldier, recruits up to 12 soldiers within 40 m who then guard (follow) the hero, and starts hunger
makes one of your own units the hero
walk order for the hero, or stop
-10 stone, creates a 4 m block in the cell within 16 m, +1 XP; refused when the cell is occupied, too far, unaffordable, or blocked (refund)
+10 stone, destroys the block within 16 m, +2 XP
stock orders for the squad: recruit, follow (guard), rally (walk in formation), attack (nearest enemy within 40 m or a target), formation, hold (stop + stand ground)
every 10 s the hero eats 1 food; with none it loses 5 hp
